title: Record reproducible native and Python dependency setup
outcome: Developers can reproduce the candidate stack and identify unsupported prerequisites before running desktop probes.
scope: Add setup instructions/scripts and a machine-readable environment report for Arch/KDE, KWin, systemd, D-Bus, libei, Python, PyGObject, dbus-python and Pillow, including resolved/native versions and maintained patches.
Pin and build/evaluate kdotool candidate be03ce90c09350898556436bac74ed35fe928617 with custom-script support; record the actual tested revision and access to distro native bindings.
Record the dependency exclusions and define which compatibility probes must rerun after each dependency changes.
acceptance: Setup and version reporting run reproducibly in the recorded target environment; missing tools/bindings produce actionable errors and bounded subprocess waits.
Reports identify exact revisions/releases and all maintained patches without inherited environment or secrets; neither ydotool nor kwin-mcp is installed, invoked or vendored, and no MCP SDK is added.

title: Build a bounded private-desktop harness and acknowledged Wayland fixture
outcome: Every adapter probe has a real private KWin session and deterministic custom-rendered application available before production implementation.
scope: Add a development harness using a transient user service, private bus/runtime/HOME/XDG and headless KWin with one 1280×720 scale-1 output; keep all ordinary children in its cgroup.

Add a minimal native Wayland fixture with custom rendering, machine-readable input acknowledgments and controllable visual state; provide a separate local test control channel to request state changes.
Bound startup and teardown, preserve generation-attributed evidence outside disposable settings, and prevent any host input/capture fallback.
acceptance: The harness opens the fixture on the private desktop without prompts; its reported output configuration is correct and it requires no viewer or accessibility metadata.
The fixture emits deterministic input receipts and signals when an intended visual change has been rendered; later screenshot checks can synchronize using that signal.

Normal completion and injected startup failure remove owned processes within a recorded provisional deadline and retain diagnostics. This harness is clearly marked as feasibility tooling, not a supported session implementation.

title: Validate kdotool structured queries and bounded focus polling
outcome: Measured evidence establishes whether pinned kdotool meets the proposed window transport contract.
scope: Create a fixed query script against the private bus for UUID/PID/title/class/client and frame geometry/active identity with explicit unavailable values and encoded dynamic data.
Probe activation followed by observed focus, vanished-window behavior, timeout/script cleanup, JSON result ordering and repeated query latency.
Record retain/replace evidence; custom JSON alone does not justify replacing kdotool.
acceptance: The real fixture is discovered without accessibility, exact client bounds are recorded and success requires observed focus rather than a successful subprocess exit.
Slow/failed queries terminate within a recorded limit and leave no query scripts/processes; measurements support a proposed bounded polling interval or record a blocker before production integration.

title: Prove the minimal libei binding and device-lifecycle test mechanism
outcome: Project-owned libei calls can negotiate usable devices, deliver acknowledged input and observe connection/device failures in the private compositor.
scope: Declare only required ctypes symbols, verify argument/return types and object/FD ownership against installed supported headers, including void ei_dispatch.
Demonstrate GLib-integrated event consumption, resumed-device gating, key press/release and cancellation with acknowledgment from the M1 fixture.

Establish a reproducible real-compositor lifecycle fault procedure for pause/removal/disconnect and reset; document any required harness extension. Record binding maintainability and known correctness issues.
acceptance: Header audit and real input evidence pass; no input is emitted on merely announced or paused devices and released keys are observed by the fixture.
A concrete fault-injection/reproduction procedure and evidence exist for lifecycle events; inability to obtain required evidence remains a blocker, not a mock-only pass.
Record measured initial cancellation/release behavior and a justified Python-versus-compiled-boundary decision; unresolved input correctness defects block the milestone.

title: Prove ScreenShot2 capture and choose the control-loop integration boundaries
outcome: All proposed adapters have feasibility evidence and measured integration decisions before production work begins.
scope: Probe private ScreenShot2 request/pipe handling with concurrent draining, metadata/pixel-format inspection, Pillow encoding and bounded FD cleanup.
Demonstrate a fresh capture after the fixture's rendered-state signal and keep blocking work outside responsive GLib event/control handling.

Record an architecture decision choosing the capture thread/process boundary and finite proposed startup/query/action/capture/stop deadlines, focus polling interval and cancellation/release bound with tested conditions; include the preceding window/libei findings.
acceptance: The private whole-output image is a complete fresh 1280×720 PNG without a viewer; partial/hung capture fails and cleans up within the proposed deadline.
Slow capture and window queries do not stall prototype event processing/cancellation. The chosen boundary identifies how blocking work is terminated or drained and owned resources are reclaimed.
A consolidated go/no-go report links reproducible evidence for every platform adapter and records any required architecture changes; unresolved feasibility blockers prevent completing M1.

title: Scaffold agent-desktop and define JSON command/error contracts
outcome: An installable Python CLI exposes explicit command contracts and stable machine-readable failures.
scope: Add packaging and command parsing for doctor; session start/status/stop; launch/windows/focus/wait; key/type/click/input reset; screenshot/logs; close/kill, with documented flags/defaults and headless mode.
Specify JSON result/error envelopes, meaningful exit statuses and stable codes for each required failure class; include request/generation identifiers, partial outcomes and handles where available.

Accept --generation on every session-addressed command; document current-generation name lookup, dispatch semantics and no automatic launch/input retry on unknown completion. Unwired operations explicitly fail.
acceptance: CLI contract checks cover success/error examples, invalid flags/arguments and unsupported commands in JSON mode; stdout has only the result and diagnostics use stderr or files.
No supported command path requires a prompt; blocking command contracts name finite worker-enforced limits, and future viewer mode does not require a backend framework.

title: Implement generation-bound Unix-socket request transport
outcome: Separate CLI invocations can address one persistent worker through a private versioned protocol with identity checked before dispatch.
scope: Define framing/version validation, bounded request reads, request IDs, operation arguments, finite timeouts and structured replies over an owner-only Unix socket.
Resolve generation-qualified session/application/window references and reject mismatches before dispatch; correlate transport failures and partial/uncertain outcomes.
Provide the worker entrypoint and transport lifecycle without retaining connections or desktop state in the CLI.
acceptance: Two independent CLI processes contact the same worker and generation; malformed/incompatible protocol and stale references produce stable errors without action side effects.
Socket/runtime permissions restrict access to the owner; worker/subprocess logs cannot enter the protocol or JSON output. A lost response is not automatically retried as launch or input.

title: Implement the responsive ordinary-action queue and cancellation channel
outcome: Ordinary actions serialize while control requests and deadlines remain responsive, including when the caller disappears.
scope: Use the chosen GLib loop and monotonic admission deadlines including queue time; express waits/actions as short cancellable steps and observe desktop subprocesses asynchronously.
Route SIGINT, client disconnect and worker timeout to the corresponding unfinished request; cancel queued work before side effects when its deadline expires.
Make cancellation, reset and stop bypass the ordinary queue and signal the owning execution context. Define cleanup continuation and result preservation for actions with partial effects.
acceptance: Deterministic task doubles demonstrate serialization, queued expiry, active cancellation, control bypass and no concurrent input-owner mutation under a slow operation.

SIGINT/socket loss cancels only the corresponding ordinary request within the provisional bound; lifecycle cleanup continues after caller departure and completed side effects are not described as undone.
Checks use worker-enforced deadlines, not just a client timeout. Later M5/M7 issues explicitly own real-adapter timing validation.

title: Implement caller-path normalization and durable generation records
outcome: CLI and worker share normalized paths and durable generation-specific manifests/log locations.
scope: Normalize relative application cwd, artifact root and screenshot output against caller cwd before transport; define omitted cwd, slash-containing executables, final PATH lookup and environment precedence.
Allocate collision-free generation/request artifact paths outside disposable settings and atomic manifest updates; define logging interfaces shared by supervisor/apps/adapters.
Record mode/output/dependency provenance, argv/cwd, process and target references, partial outcomes, cleanup status and terminal outcome, without dumping credentials or the inherited environment.
acceptance: Checks from a directory different from the worker verify all relative/default path cases and executable-resolution contracts.
Repeated allocations do not collide, interrupted manifest writes preserve a valid prior record, and all required schema fields have defined producers.
A simulated failed startup/terminal cleanup retains artifact records and preserves an already-recorded failure; M3/M6 wire the real producers and artifact access.

title: Implement generation-owned transient service start and idempotent lifecycle
outcome: Session names resolve to distinct service generations that cannot be confused across start/stop races.
scope: Serialize per-name start/stop decisions, bind service and runtime paths to random immutable generations and compare all supported configuration for duplicate starts.
Launch the persistent worker in a transient user service with no automatic restart, KillMode=control-group and finite TimeoutStopSec; retain service identity for fallback stop.
Guard manager-side start/status/stop and runtime removal with expected-generation checks, including when the worker socket is unavailable.
acceptance: Repeated compatible start returns the same identity, conflicting start fails, stopped stop succeeds and restarting the same name produces a new generation.
Concurrent lifecycle/race checks show stale start/stop requests cannot stop or remove a replacement generation, including the unresponsive-worker path.
Separate CLI invocations retain a live session; systemd owns ordinary descendants and records use the correct generation.

title: Construct the private desktop and protected application environment
outcome: Private KWin, adapters and trusted applications receive explicit isolated desktop/settings endpoints.
scope: Create owner-only runtime/control storage and disposable HOME/XDG settings, launch observed private D-Bus and KWin children with one headless 1280×720 scale-1 output.

Centralize application environment construction: strip host DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY/Wayland/D-Bus/accessibility endpoints, apply allowed overrides, then install private protected settings and reject protected overrides.
Keep host user-manager access confined to lifecycle control and any EIS/ScreenShot2 permission adjustments confined to the created compositor; retain trusted project/network access.
acceptance: A real environment-reporting child has the intended private endpoints/settings and can read its project files; protected override attempts fail before launch.
Contaminated host environment tests show neither adapters nor applications fall back to personal display/accessibility/clipboard endpoints; runtime sockets/files are owner-only.
No global KDE configuration is changed; private settings are disposable and artifact roots remain outside them.

title: Gate readiness on capabilities and monitor essential-process health
outcome: Session state reflects live capabilities and essential process health instead of persisted files alone.
scope: Implement starting/ready/stopping/stopped/failed states and monitor worker service, bus and compositor health.
Require control connectivity, structured window query, resumed input device and screenshot probe before ready; adapt the real M1 probes behind interfaces until production adapters arrive in M7.1.
Bound readiness/subprocess/pipe waits; reject desktop work on essential failure and initiate the cleanup path. Supply structured health/prerequisite details for doctor/status.
acceptance: Socket appearance alone cannot make the session ready; each missing capability causes a specific startup failure with retained diagnostics.
Independent bus/compositor death and worker death/unresponsiveness produce unavailable status based on live observations and reject further work.
Probe timeout and status checks obey finite deadlines; tests name the production replacement owned by M7.1 so provisional readiness cannot pass release qualification.

title: Implement graceful shutdown orchestration and crash-independent cgroup cleanup
outcome: Stop and essential failures clean ordinary descendants within a finite deadline even when the worker or client cannot cooperate.
scope: Order shutdown hooks as cancellation, tracked release, normal application-window close, then service-manager termination of remaining owned processes within the overall shutdown budget.
Implement a bounded service cleanup hook that records terminal outcome and removes only generation-owned runtime/settings files, preserving earlier failures and durable artifacts.

Cover startup failure and independent worker/compositor/private-bus death, worker hang, and client disconnect; use the manager fallback when socket control is unusable. Production app/input hooks are wired in M7.1.
acceptance: Real ordinary child/grandchild processes disappear within the shutdown bound after normal stop, failed start and each essential-process failure, including a blocked worker.
Hook-order checks prove release/close are attempted before escalation; no client connection is required for cleanup to finish.
Stale hooks cannot touch replacement-generation files/services; artifacts and a truthful final manifest survive worker death before it can record its outcome.

title: Launch argv workloads with durable ownership and a one-active-application limit
outcome: A launch is tracked from process creation through exit, including descendants, timeout and cancellation.
scope: Launch argument vectors without an implicit shell using normalized cwd, final application PATH and protected environment construction; allocate logs and an application ID before observable side effects where possible.

Track kernel-backed process identities, exit status and ordinary descendants using a documented reliable ownership mechanism; retain handles/results if subsequent processing or the client connection fails. Expose retention hooks for the real window waits implemented in M4.3.

Enforce one active application per session, including tracked living descendants; allow its dialogs and a later sequential launch after the tracked process set exits. Extend the fixture with exits, delayed windows and descendants.
acceptance: Different-cwd tests verify executable paths, bare PATH lookup, argv boundaries, explicit allowed environment overrides and durable stdout/stderr logs.

A simulated post-launch wait failure, cancellation and a disconnected real launch retain the application/process handle and known side effects in records; no automatic launch retry occurs. Real compositor window-timeout acceptance belongs to M4.3, after discovery/waits exist.

A second launch while the first app or its descendants remains live fails before spawning; a later launch after complete exit succeeds. Ownership records cannot become signaling authority for a reused PID.

title: Implement asynchronous structured KWin window discovery
outcome: Window snapshots carry compositor identity and geometry without relying on titles or accessibility metadata.
scope: Promote the pinned kdotool fixed-script probe to a typed adapter on explicit private D-Bus endpoints; asynchronously supervise each subprocess with deadlines and script cleanup.
Return generation-scoped KWin identity, PID, title/class, client/frame bounds and active focus, representing unavailable metadata explicitly.

Safely encode data instead of accepting caller JavaScript and associate windows with verified owned application processes. Extend the fixture with dialogs, duplicate titles and unavailable/unassociated metadata cases where feasible.
acceptance: Real custom-rendered windows/dialogs return expected identities and client geometry without accessibility; duplicate titles remain distinct candidates.
Unassociated windows are exposed without false ownership claims; malformed adapter output and slow/hung queries fail explicitly and do not block control-loop cancellation.
Query subprocess/script resources are reclaimed on error, timeout and cancellation; dynamic values cannot become arbitrary script source.

title: Implement unambiguous target resolution, verified focus and bounded waits
outcome: Targeting and waits use current compositor state and return distinct, actionable outcomes.
scope: Resolve explicit identity or a unique owned-application association; return candidates on ambiguity, reject vanished/stale-generation references and recheck at execution after queue delay.
Implement focus as activation followed by bounded observation of the exact active window; provide reusable existence/focus/current-geometry checks for input.
Add bounded window/focus/app-exit waits that distinguish timeout, application exit, cancellation and failed session and retain launch handles on window timeout.
acceptance: Identical-title dialogs force explicit selection; windows that vanish or move while queued are revalidated before side effects.
Activation subprocess success without observed focus fails or times out; waits cover each documented outcome against the real fixture.
Focus queries honor the chosen deadline and return fresh client geometry suitable for click translation; no title-based identity fallback occurs.

title: Implement graceful window close without implicit escalation
outcome: Close requests normal window closure and reports application exit while leaving confirmation dialogs under caller control.
scope: Wire close to explicit/unique target resolution, request normal KWin window closure and wait within the shared deadline for tracked application exit.
Extend the real fixture with close confirmation and refusal/delay cases; return application/window references and remaining process state on timeout.
Expose a reusable bounded close hook for session shutdown while keeping explicit close semantics independent of shutdown escalation.
acceptance: Normal close reports observed application exit; a confirmation dialog remains open and discoverable for explicit subsequent input.
Close timeout does not send signals, auto-dismiss dialogs or report application exit merely because a window closed. Vanished and ambiguous targets return documented errors.

title: Implement explicit termination of verified application processes
outcome: The separate kill command terminates only verified owned processes and accurately reports remaining descendants.
scope: Define the finite explicit termination sequence and use tracked kernel process identities and descendant ownership instead of saved PID authority.
Wait for the tracked application process set, including descendants after original-parent exit, and return exited/remaining process outcomes.
Add PID-reuse/ownership-race checks and real child/grandchild lifetime cases; distinguish application termination from session-wide systemd cleanup.
acceptance: A reused PID or unowned process is never signaled; generation mismatch fails before termination begins.
Real tracked descendants are terminated or explicitly reported as remaining within the deadline, and subsequent wait/status sees correct exit state.
Calling kill is explicit; launch, wait and graceful close failures cannot invoke it automatically.

title: Implement the persistent libei connection and resumed-device lifecycle
outcome: One worker execution context owns a header-checked private EIS/libei connection and continuously updated device readiness.
scope: Promote the M1 binding to a limited production module with verified ctypes signatures, explicit object/FD ownership and GLib event integration.
Negotiate EIS only through the private compositor, consume events continuously and gate emission on usable resumed devices.
On pause/removal/disconnect mark affected devices unusable, notify the active action to cancel and record release uncertainty; expose readiness/reconnect hooks for reset and startup.
acceptance: Real event traces demonstrate negotiation and resumed readiness before input; events continue to be consumed during ordinary actions and slow external work.
The M1 real-compositor fault procedure exercises pause/removal/connection loss with explicit unavailable errors and resource cleanup; no stale-ready or host fallback path exists.
Native declarations/ownership are checked against the recorded headers and no known correctness defect remains; tests supplement but do not replace real lifecycle evidence.

title: Implement fully validated physical keys, chords, text and finite holds
outcome: Supported input requests compile into finite press/release sequences before any emission.
scope: Document physical-key names including common game keys, legal chord structure, finite hold limits and the supported US-layout character set.
Prevalidate the complete request and generate short sequence steps; track explicit keys/buttons and modifiers generated for text, with a release ledger shared by completion/cancellation/reset.
Extend fixture acknowledgments for key order, modifier state, text and hold duration; expose dispatch results without claiming application rendering.
acceptance: Supported text/chords/game keys and finite holds are received by the real fixture in the expected order and all normal-completion releases are observed.
Unsupported characters anywhere in text, invalid chord keys or invalid/nonfinite holds reject the entire request before emitting any input.
No public operation can leave an indefinite key-down state across commands; the ledger includes generated modifiers and identifies uncertain effects.

title: Enforce window focus and current client-coordinate targeting for every input action
outcome: Input executes only after current target checks, with finite rechecks during repeated or held input and correctly translated clicks.
scope: Require explicit or unambiguously resolved window identity for key/type/click, confirm existence and verified focus before emission and revalidate after queue delay.
Schedule bounded focus/existence polls during sequences/holds using asynchronous queries; stop further input on lost target/focus or a timed-out check.
Prevalidate click button/coordinates, then check current client-content bounds and translate to output coordinates excluding decorations immediately before dispatch.
acceptance: Real fixture clicks at valid client edges reach the expected content positions; negative/out-of-range coordinates fail without emission and moving/resizing queued targets uses new geometry.
Focus theft and vanished windows cancel held/repeated input within the measured polling bound; a slow or timed-out query never permits continued input using stale focus.
All input commands reject missing/ambiguous/stale targets, and documentation states checked focus-based behavior and its non-atomic compositor race limit.

title: Guarantee bounded input cancellation and tracked release on every exit path
outcome: Cancellation stops further emission and attempts all tracked releases within a measured bound, without queueing behind an active action.
scope: Connect the single input owner to completion, SIGINT, client loss, worker timeout, focus/target loss, device failure and shutdown cancellation paths.
Use short steps and timers, stop future sequence work, release tracked keys/buttons/modifiers and preserve partial/uncertain effects and handles in replies/logs.

Extend the harness for cancellation during holds and shifted typing with slow asynchronous queries and controlled external work using the M1 capture harness or a delay double; collect emission-stop and release-attempt timing evidence. Production capture responsiveness belongs to M7.4. Preserve ordinary-action serialization: test active input and active capture scenarios separately, including cancellation of queued work.
acceptance: Separate CLI interruption/disconnection and worker-enforced timeout meet the documented bound during real holds and modified text; fixture receipts show no continuing sequence after cancellation detection.
Normal completion and every failure path attempt release; an unconfirmable release is reported and blocks further input rather than silently clearing the ledger.
Control bypass works under queued requests and slow desktop calls, with no concurrent libei mutation and no automatic retry or claim that earlier side effects were undone.

title: Implement input reset and recovery from uncertain release
outcome: Explicit reset recovers a usable private input connection or leaves input unavailable with truthful diagnostics.
scope: Make reset bypass the action queue, ask the input owner to cancel active input first, then release tracked state or replace the private connection.
Wait for newly usable resumed devices before reporting reset success; clean up old connection resources and never replay interrupted input.
Provide production release/reset hooks for M7.1 startup/shutdown integration and exercise the established real lifecycle failure procedures.
acceptance: Reset during a held key cancels the active sequence and restores usable input only after safe release/reconnection; a subsequent targeted action is acknowledged correctly.
Connection loss with uncertain release blocks new input until successful reset or session stop, and a failed reset leaves it blocked.
Pause/removal/disconnect and repeated reset attempts do not leak connection resources or publish readiness early; reset/stop remain responsive during active input.

title: Implement bounded private ScreenShot2 transport and pixel decoding
outcome: Fresh whole-output pixel data arrives through a validated private capture path that cannot block worker control handling.
scope: Implement explicit private-bus ScreenShot2 calls, concurrent pipe draining during pending replies, supported metadata/stride/pixel-format validation and Pillow decoding.
Use the M1-selected execution boundary with enforced deadlines, cancellation and owned pipe/descriptor/task cleanup; disallow personal-desktop fallback.
Return typed complete image data or stable capture/unsupported/timeout/session errors with side-effect context.
acceptance: Real headless captures produce correctly decoded whole-output dimensions/colors after the M1 fixture's rendered-state signal.
Truncated data, invalid metadata/unsupported formats, hung producer, bus death and cancellation fail within the bound and reclaim owned resources.
Slow capture cannot stall control/health processing; a disconnected client does not abandon the adapter's required cleanup.

title: Publish unique complete PNG artifacts and screenshot metadata
outcome: Each successful screenshot identifies a newly captured fully written PNG and its generation/provenance.
scope: Wire screenshot CLI to fresh capture, a unique temporary output, Pillow PNG encoding and atomic complete-file publication; define safe behavior for an already-existing explicit destination.
Resolve destinations at the calling CLI and return absolute path, dimensions, capture timestamp, backend and generation only after writing completes.
Keep failed temporary images distinguishable from completed artifacts and preserve earlier screenshots across stop/failure.
acceptance: Repeated requests yield distinct fresh complete 1280×720 PNGs; fixture-acknowledged visual changes appear and no previous image is returned as a new capture.
Disk/write failure, cancellation and partial capture cannot publish a partial PNG as success or destroy an earlier artifact; output paths work from a different caller cwd.
JSON stdout is clean and results/documentation make no claim that prior input has been acknowledged or rendered without an application-specific signal.

title: Wire artifact discovery, correlated logs and complete durable manifests
outcome: Users can locate generation-attributed diagnostics and understand failed runs after the session runtime has been removed.
scope: Wire the logs command and artifact index to generation-specific durable storage, with a documented way to inspect stopped/failed-generation artifacts and generation checks on session-addressed requests.
Connect helper/compositor/bus/capture producers to the M2 manifest/logging API and integrate app records when M4 is available; M7.1 verifies the final complete schema.
Correlate request IDs, application/window handles and screenshot paths; retain dependency revisions/patches, argv/cwd, mode/geometry, final outcome and cleanup diagnostics without credentials.
acceptance: Logs/artifacts for stopped and failed startup sessions remain discoverable and cannot be confused with a same-name replacement generation.
Manifest completeness checks verify each required field's producer, preserve prior failure outcomes and validate collision-free artifacts; application fields are exercised with M4 records in M7.1.
Inspecting artifacts cannot alter session state or pollute JSON output with application logs; screenshots and logs survive runtime/settings deletion.

title: Connect production adapters to readiness, doctor and shutdown
outcome: All CLI commands and session lifecycle checks use production behavior with no provisional readiness or shutdown hooks.
scope: Replace M3's probe adapters with production control/window/resumed-input/fresh-capture probes and wire actual app-close and input-release hooks into bounded shutdown.
Complete doctor checks for installed versions, user-manager availability and private desktop capabilities, with actionable errors and finite limits.
Audit command wiring, stable error mapping, partial outcomes and manifest producers across components; enforce noninteractive operation and cleanup independent of the client.
acceptance: Ready is impossible unless every production probe succeeds; failure in any probe retains diagnostics and invokes bounded cleanup.
Stop attempts actual release and graceful close before cgroup escalation; hung/dead helper fallback still works and records truthful outcomes.
Every documented command family has a real successful or explicitly unsupported path with valid JSON/errors, and manifests contain all required actual launch/dependency/terminal data.

title: Assemble the real-desktop workflow integration suite
outcome: A repeatable automated workflow verifies input and visible results against the real private KWin desktop through separate CLI processes.
scope: Assemble the existing M1/M4/M5 fixtures and harness with one CLI process per action: doctor/start, launch, discover, focus, capture, type, chord/hold/release, click, close and stop.
Wait on fixture input acknowledgments and rendered-state signals before expected pixel checks; assert complete PNG metadata and retained application logs/handles.
Include graceful-close confirmation, explicit termination and window/focus/exit waits, caller-relative path cases and output isolation in the reusable suite.
acceptance: The full workflow passes on the recorded real target environment and proves expected input receipts plus visual change; mocks alone cannot satisfy it.
Every run records environment, generations, requests and artifacts and checks no owned processes or held input remain at teardown.
A required unavailable platform capability is a failed qualification prerequisite, not a silent skip; the harness is reusable for the twenty-run gate.

title: Verify lifecycle, identity, environment and target failure contracts
outcome: Automated failures establish generation safety, honest target/process outcomes and cleanup independent of essential processes.
scope: Create an explicit REQ-038 case index and exercise stale generations after restart, start/stop races, duplicate/conflicting starts, ambiguous/vanished targets and application exit versus window timeout.
Independently kill worker/compositor/private bus, hang the worker and fail startup; verify unavailable status, client-independent bounded descendant cleanup and durable terminal artifacts.
Check contaminated host endpoints, protected overrides, different caller cwd, PID reuse, surviving descendants, close confirmation/timeout and explicit-kill remaining-process reporting.
acceptance: Each listed failure has an identified test and retained evidence; stale commands/fallback cleanup cannot affect a replacement generation or unrelated process.
Each essential-process failure leaves no ordinary owned descendants after its deadline, preserves original failure diagnostics and rejects later desktop work.
Environment/path tests establish separation and no host fallback. Application handles and uncertain outcomes remain available after timeout/cancellation without automatic retries.

title: Verify cancellation, device faults and capture responsiveness against measured bounds
outcome: Production evidence proves input stopping/release attempts and control responsiveness during slow or failed desktop operations.
scope: Complete the REQ-038 index with unsupported full text/chords, focus loss, vanished input targets, SIGINT/disconnect and worker timeout during holds and modified typing.

Exercise real device pause/removal/disconnect using the established procedure, uncertain release, reset during active work and failed reset; supplement with deterministic edge-case doubles only where appropriate.

Inject slow/timed-out focus queries and blocked/partial capture, queued deadline expiry and stop/reset while active; measure polling, emission-stop/release-attempt, capture and cleanup limits under recorded conditions.
acceptance: Each required case meets the documented finite bound and records actual timing; failures require fixes or explicitly revised measured limits before support, never silent acceptance.
Unsupported requests emit nothing, uncertain release blocks input, failed reset stays unavailable and successful reset waits for resumed devices without replay.

Slow capture/query work cannot starve cancellation/stop/health handling, resources are reclaimed and partial images are never successful artifacts; the complete REQ-038 index is satisfied with real lifecycle evidence.

title: Document reproducible setup, CLI workflows and measured support semantics
outcome: A user can install the recorded stack, run a smoke workflow and understand targeting, timing and recovery behavior.
scope: Write setup and CLI reference with JSON examples, explicit flags/defaults, cwd/PATH/env precedence, protected endpoints, generation-qualified handles and durable artifact retrieval.
Publish measured deadlines/cancellation and focus polling limits with tested conditions, supported physical keys/chords/US text, client coordinates and reset/uncertain-release troubleshooting.
Provide a repeatable real-desktop smoke command and supported-versus-deferred scope, trusted filesystem/network access and dispatch-versus-acknowledgment/rendering semantics.
acceptance: Reproduce installation and the documented workflow from a clean project environment with the required native packages; operations are noninteractive after prerequisite setup.
Examples work from a different directory and preserve generations across invocations; smoke output identifies artifacts and meaningful failures.
Docs name measured limits and dependency revisions, avoid unsupported application promises, and explain the compatibility checks required after dependency changes.

title: Pass twenty consecutive full CLI workflows in the recorded target environment
outcome: The first supported version has reproducible consecutive-run reliability evidence for its final implementation and dependencies.
scope: Run the M7 workflow twenty consecutive times in the recorded Arch/KDE target, preserving per-run logs/screenshots/manifests, timing and dependency provenance.
Assert no unexpected prompts, stuck input or leftover owned processes after every run; retain failure history and restart the consecutive count after fixes.
Confirm the full M7 failure suite is passing on the qualified build, and rerun affected compatibility/failure checks after dependency or code changes.
acceptance: A report links twenty uninterrupted passing runs of the complete separate-CLI workflow and per-run teardown/input checks, not merely twenty compositor starts.
All MUST failure conditions have current passing evidence; failures/environment limitations remain recorded and required checks are not silently skipped.
The evidence identifies the exact qualified code revision and resolved target environment; later relevant changes invalidate affected evidence until rerun.

title: Record representative application validation and close requirement coverage
outcome: Published support claims match recorded application evidence and every required behavior has an implementation/test reference.
scope: Select a representative native Wayland app/game relevant to the user's workflow at implementation time; record a successful supported workflow and exact app/environment versions, or document a reasoned REQ-044 exception and consequences.
Publish a requirement-to-code/test/evidence index for every MUST and disposition for each SHOULD, including reuse choices, diagnostics, configuration and future-viewing compatibility.
Review the twenty-run report and docs, record remaining environment limitations and explicitly defer REQ-047–050 and all outside-first-version features.
acceptance: Every REQ-001–040 has passing implementation/validation evidence; every REQ-041–046 is satisfied or has an explicit reason and consequences for an exception.
Support is claimed only for recorded successful native app/environment combinations; an optional representative-app exception cannot waive any MUST or the twenty-run gate.
No live-viewer, XWayland, richer input/output/multiple-app, MCP, sandbox or general game support commitment slips into the initial release; relevant post-qualification changes trigger revalidation.
